t: The first recorded meeting between Teotihuacan and the Maya took place at Waka' in January 378, when the war leader Siyaj K'ahk' passed through roughly eight to ten days before taking over Tikal: the moment archaeologists call La Entrada.

Waka' abandoned its early alliance with Tikal for Calakmul, sealed by the marriage of K'inich Balam to a princess of the Kan dynasty who bore the high title ix kaloomté; Lady K'abel governed the Wak kingdom for the Snake dynasty between 672 and 692.

Tikal's ruler Yik'in Chan K'awiil defeated Waka' in 743, made it a vassal and carried off an image of a celestial serpent, possibly its patron deity; a decade later the city was destroyed and K'inich Balam's successor captured and sacrificed.
dyk: Burial 39, the tomb of an early seventh-century king, held 23 ceramic figurines of a royal court at a ceremony, among them a kneeling king with the Maize God's hair, a female singer conjuring a deer spirit, a dwarf blowing a shell trumpet and two helmeted dwarfs who may be boxers.
ev: The Teotihuacan war leader Siyaj K'ahk' arrives at Waka' in January, ten days before reaching Tikal: La Entrada, the first recorded meeting of Teotihuacan and the Maya.
Waka' reaches its political peak with a population of tens of thousands, drawn by its location and trade.
Stela 15, a text-only monument, is erected naming the kings back to the mid fourth century and recording Siyaj K'ahk's coming.
Lady K'abel, daughter of Calakmul's king Yuknoom Yich'aak K'ak' and wife of K'inich B'ahlam II, governs the Wak kingdom as a lady warlord for the Kan dynasty.
Stela 34 portrays Lady K'abel; her tomb, found in the main pyramid temple in 2012, held an alabaster jar naming Lady Water Lily Hand and Lady Snake Lord.
Calakmul's ruler Yuknoom Took' K'awiil, likely the brother of Lady T'abi, is defeated, captured and sacrificed in Tikal's central plaza.
Yik'in Chan K'awiil of Tikal defeats Waka', makes it a vassal and takes the image of its celestial serpent to Tikal, recorded on Temple IV.
About a decade after its defeat Waka' is destroyed and K'inich Balam's successor is captured and sacrificed.

f.capital: Waka' (El Perú), on an escarpment six kilometres north of the San Pedro River in the Petén of northern Guatemala
f.predecessor: The Preclassic settlement at the site, occupied from roughly 500 BCE
f.successor: A vassal of Tikal from 743; the city was destroyed about a decade later and its occupation ended around 800
